fixes.explanation: Aaron is named in this passage, friend, because God tells Moses to speak to him and his sons. But he's not the one making anybody holy here. God says, "I am the LORD who sanctifies them." (Leviticus 22:9) The One giving the charge is the One doing the sanctifying.
Firstborn is a good guess, baker, but it isn't the word in this verse. Here the offering must be "…an unblemished male from the cattle, sheep, or goats…" (Leviticus 22:19) The word God uses is male.

That one's false, baker. God says the peace offering "…must be without blemish or defect to be acceptable." (Leviticus 22:21) There's no room for a small blemish. It's the same standard the burnt offering gets in Leviticus 22:19-20, where God says anything with a defect "will not be accepted on your behalf."

Good thinking, baker, but this verse doesn't mention a Nazirite. God says, "Neither you nor a foreigner shall present food to your God from any such animal." (Leviticus 22:25) The one named here is the foreigner.
Canaan is a fair guess, friend, but it's not the land named here. God says He "…brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God." (Leviticus 22:33) The land He brought them out of is Egypt.

Babylon is a name you'll find in the Bible, baker, but it isn't the land in this verse. God says He "…brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God." (Leviticus 22:33) The land He brought them out of is Egypt.
